solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Broadcast equipment is something that needs no feed?

parts.note: to broadcast a programme is to air it
plant is heavy industrial machinery or equipment

explanation.surface: A radio engineer's kit described as somehow needing no power cable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feed' looks like a signal feed for the broadcast gear; it is plant food. An air plant (epiphyte) draws its nourishment from the air rather than soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Epiphytes such as tillandsias live without soil, taking moisture and nutrients from the atmosphere, so they need no feeding.

clue.text: No simian suffers inability to doze

indicators.note: the letters suffer, being knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: No ape is ever troubled by sleeplessness.
explanation.definitionFit: This condition is chronic sleeplessness, being unable to drop off.

clue.text: Pomposity of pensioner worked up about the ending of Brexit

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the final letter
the word pensioner is worked into a new shape
only the last letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: An elderly person gets self-important and agitated about the end of Brexit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked up' rearranges PENSIONER to PRE+ENSION, which goes 'about' T, the end of Brexit.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretension is a claim to more importance or merit than one has, which is pomposity.

clue.text: Self-guided car — no timid person's wanting key

parts.note: auto is short for automobile

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is missing

parts.note: a mouse is a timid person
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A self-driving car with no nervous driver needing an ignition key.
explanation.definitionFit: Autonomous means self-governing, acting independently, as in a driverless vehicle.

clue.text: Expedition allowed to make notes

parts.note: a trip is a journey or expedition
let means allowed

explanation.surface: An explorer is permitted to keep a journal on the voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' suggests jotting; it is music, three notes played in the time of two.
explanation.definitionFit: In music this is a group of three notes played in the time of two.

clue.text: Clutch engages only intermittently

indicators.note: only every other letter is used, as in something working on and off

explanation.surface: A car's clutch that only catches now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clutch' looks like the pedal; it is a set laid by a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A clutch is a set of eggs laid at one time by a bird.

clue.text: Company getting support for office equipment

parts.note: a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge or arch

explanation.surface: A firm gets funding for new office machines.
explanation.definitionFit: A photocopier is a standard machine in offices.

clue.text: Like some waltzing couples starting vigorous energetic new sequence

indicators.note: the opening pair of letters of each word is taken

explanation.surface: Dancers launching a lively new routine.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'starting' takes the first two letters of each word, not one.
explanation.definitionFit: Vienna is the home of the waltz, so dancers of the Strauss style are from that city.

clue.text: Equipment engaged in working one type of extruded tubes

parts.note: a rig is a set of equipment, as in a drilling rig
to be at something is to be busy with it, as in 'at work'
a machine that is on is working
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Describes some machine busy at work producing tubes in a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: This pasta is short ridged tubes made by pushing dough through a die, a classic extruded shape.

clue.text: Exactly how things were dispatched for approval

parts.note: 'as' means in the way that, as in 'leave it as it is'
dispatched goods have been sent

explanation.surface: A shipping clerk confirms that goods went out exactly as ordered, getting sign-off.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part reads as the phrase 'as sent', the way a delivery note confirms goods went out unaltered.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving one's agreement or consent to a proposal is the same as giving approval.

clue.text: Work site creates resistance

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
a site is a location or position

explanation.surface: Building work on a site stirs up local protest.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposition is the act of resisting or the people resisting, so it means resistance.

clue.text: Soon cutting intro from French opera

indicators.note: the introduction, the first letter, is cut away from the opera's title

parts.note: Manon is Massenet's French opera

explanation.surface: An instruction to trim a French opera's overture quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old word for shortly or presently, as in 'I'll see you anon'.

clue.text: Ask too much throughout career

parts.note: 'over' can mean throughout, as in 'over the years'
to career is to rush headlong, to charge

explanation.surface: Someone has been demanding excessive fees for their whole working life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' looks like a noun, a working life; here it is the verb to rush, i.e. charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To overcharge is to demand a higher price than is fair, asking too much money.

clue.text: Communication's lost at exchange

indicators.note: the word 'at' is lost from the longer word

parts.note: a conversation is a form of communication; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: A message goes astray at a telephone exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: Converting currency is exchanging it, as in a foreign-currency conversion.

clue.text: A talk about time, missing energy and strange particles

indicators.note: the chatter goes around the shortened time

parts.note: natter is idle talk

indicators.note: missing means the letter is left out

parts.note: taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A physics lecture on time, with energy left out, about weird particles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops E from TIME to give TIM, and NATTER goes 'about' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiparticles such as positrons are strange counterparts of ordinary particles, with opposite charge.

clue.text: Soldier dropped in to Vietnam returned as Minister of War

indicators.note: the soldier is dropped inside the other letters, like a paratrooper
the words to and Vietnam are read backwards

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An American paratrooper sent into Vietnam comes home to become a cabinet minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns TO NAM into MANOT, and GI is dropped in to give the name.
explanation.definitionFit: André Maginot was France's Minister of War, remembered for the defensive line named after him.

clue.text: Painter of river in haze

indicators.note: the river is placed inside the haze

parts.note: mist is a haze
the Ural is a river in Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: An artist painting a river shrouded in mist.
explanation.definitionFit: This artist paints large works directly on walls.

clue.text: At no particular moment very soon

definitions.meaning: whenever you like, with no fixed time
as in 'he'll be here any minute now'

explanation.surface: Two descriptions of when something will happen.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means at whatever time one likes, and also, as in 'it's due any time now', imminently.

clue.text: Designer using a lot of cutting to top off Queen?

indicators.note: in a down entry, the shortened word sits on top of the Queen
most of the word is used, the last letter dropped

parts.note: milling is cutting or shaping metal on a machine
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A hat designer who trims and cuts to crown a Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The '?' nods to the surface: hats top off a queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A milliner designs and makes women's hats.

clue.text: Religious leader has power over words

parts.note: 'on' can mean over, about
to have words is to quarrel, a tiff

explanation.surface: A church leader holds sway over sacred texts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pope is called the Supreme Pontiff, the head of the Catholic Church.

clue.text: Artificial shiner with quality?

indicators.note: something artificial is made up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: tone is the quality of a sound or colour

explanation.surface: A fake sparkler that still has a touch of class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artificial' rearranges SHINER into RHINES; the whole clue also describes the paste gem itself.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a glittering imitation diamond, a fake gem that shines and gives costume jewellery its quality.

clue.text: What might be made on raid

definitions.text: What might be made on raid

indicators.note: the letters are made into a new word

explanation.surface: Asks what an attacking force achieves on a raid.
explanation.definitionFit: An attacking force makes a hostile advance into enemy territory during an incursion.

clue.text: Well out of East African country

indicators.note: the word for well is taken out of the other word

parts.note: Somali describes something from Somalia in East Africa
'so' is used like 'well' to start a remark

explanation.surface: A water well dug in an East African nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East African country' wants to be one definition, but the country is West African: East African gives SOMALI.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked nation in West Africa, capital Bamako.

clue.text: Sit angrily, disposed to make a complaint

indicators.note: the letters are disposed, laid out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone sits sulking, inclined to make a grievance known.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' looks like a grievance; it is an ailment, inflammation of the voice box.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint in the medical sense is an illness, and inflammation of the voice box is one.

clue.text: Develop good argument

parts.note: a row is a noisy argument

explanation.surface: A sound debate helps someone mature.
explanation.definitionFit: To develop is to increase in size or mature, which is growing.

clue.text: Aim to complete after opening bid?

indicators.note: the word for complete comes after the bid

parts.note: in bridge, 1NT (one no trump) is a standard opening bid, read here as INT
to end something is to complete it

explanation.surface: A player aims to finish the job after making the first bid at auction.
explanation.walkthrough: In the card game bridge, 1NT (one no trump) is a common opening bid; the 1 doubles as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To intend something is to have it as one's purpose, to aim to do it.

clue.text: When new function is introduced, employees keep away

indicators.note: the new letters are put into the word for employees

parts.note: the staff are the employees
a do is a party or social function

explanation.surface: Staff boycott the launch of a new software feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'function' looks like computing; it is a do, a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand off is to hold back at a distance, to keep away.

clue.text: Anger about November period for a ceremony for the dead

definitions.text: for a ceremony for the dead

indicators.note: the word for anger goes around the others

parts.note: fury is great anger
N is November in the phonetic alphabet
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Grief turns to rage around Remembrance month at a memorial service.
explanation.definitionFit: Funerary describes things relating to funerals and burial, the rites for the deceased.
